correctness.rationale: For positive temperatures, 0<u<1 and independent full Poisson resets with centered marks of covariance mI, conditioning on the last reset gives the stationary OU mixture. The shifted Lyapunov equation has a unique solution and diagonal difference 2(T_y−T_x)/(r+2). The conditional future mean e^{−(A+rI)τ}Z_t gives C_r(τ)=C_r e^{−(A+rI)τ} (A symmetric); negative lags transpose. In the high-rate limit the age and noise go to zero in probability and g is bounded and continuous at the mark almost surely since R>0. Put W=R² and f=E[cos(2Θ)|W]. The exact attainable set of f is |f|≤1 with E[Wf]=0: conditional antipodal axis masses implement every such f and give zero cross moment and zero mean. The qualifier E[Wf]=0 is implicit from the preceding constraint and is needed in the implementation paragraph. For an explicit optimizer, use a median b>0 of the probability law with weight W/EW and let f be +1 below b, −1 above b, balancing its value at b. Then E[Wf]=0 and E[f]=E|1−W/b|. The upper bound E[f]≤E|1−aW| for every a≥0, followed by sign flip and scaling, proves the entire closed interval, including atoms and single-radius laws. At the two specified radii, the weighted masses are both 9/10; the dual objective is 4/5 on [1/9,1]. For r=5000 the norm drift/noise bound is at most 9/10000+sqrt(12/5000), giving error strictly below 509/1250 in E[g] and opposite angular velocities beyond ±491/2500, while L=2/5002 for both. The zero-reset Gaussian integral is strictly positive because the diagonal difference is T_y−T_x>0. Writing Ω(r) as r times the Laplace transform of the bounded fixed-age angular expectation also gives real analyticity for r>0; opposite signs therefore entail a strict crossing, not a zero plateau. The observable is the specified continuous-flight forward mean, not winding or jump rotation.
